ArXiv cs.AI.title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18642v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down. We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. ArXiv cs.AI.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18714v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18747v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior.

ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18793v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Purpose: Multimodal medical imaging fusion (MMIF) is an increasingly important approach to breast cancer detection (BCD), as different imaging modalities rely on different physical principles and provide complementary information. No single modality can capture all the structural, functional, and biological information needed for accurate diagnosis and characterization. ArXiv cs.AI.title: D\'ecoupage: Directorial Audio-Visual Control for Long Multi-Shot Video Generation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18866v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In cinematic storytelling, sound and visual transitions do not always coincide in lockstep: dialogue frequently bridges across cuts to reveal reactions or introduces new scenes via J- and L-cuts, while deliberate silences pace the scene. Existing audio-visual generative frameworks, however, lack explicit mechanisms to coordinate independent visual and acoustic timing over extended horizons. ArXiv cs.AI.title: SPLICE: Structured Prompt Local Iterative Combinatorial Evolution
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18883v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Natural language optimization (NLO) improves an agent by having a model critique and rewrite its natural language policy parameters: system prompts, tool instructions, reasoning directives, few-shot demonstrations. These artifacts are multi-section documents in which some sections encode contracts (safety clauses, tool schemas, output formats) that must not drift, while others are legitimate optimization targets. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Bring Back Language to Actions: Restoring VLM capabilities in VLA Models via Parameter Merging
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18891v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) are obtained by fine-tuning pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on robot demonstration data, enabling action prediction from visual observations and language instructions. However, this fine-tuning induces catastrophic forgetting, substantially degrading the semantic and visual grounding capabilities of the original VLM. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Ask Precisely, Assume Wisely: Interactive Evaluation of Ambiguity Resolution in Large Language Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18905v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ambiguity is a core challenge in human--AI interaction, where models must decide when to make assumptions and when to seek clarification. Existing approaches to ambiguity evaluation largely focus on coverage over multiple interpretations using static metrics, offering limited insight into how efficiently a model converges toward a single user-intended interpretation through interaction. ArXiv cs.AI.title: MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18908v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Between Rigor and Reality: How AI Safety Benchmark Developers Understand Benchmark Use and Maintenance
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18930v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Safety benchmarks are cited as the primary tool to understand the risks posed by generative AI (GenAI) systems, yet growing evidence suggests they often fail to meet the needs of real-world safety evaluation. We present findings from five interviews with AI safety benchmark developers in academia and industry. We find a disconnect between perceptions of the intended usefulness of safety benchmarks and their practical usefulness in safety evaluations of deployed systems. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Dual-Stage Channel-Posterior Integration for MLM-Aided Token Communications
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18958v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Token transmission over conventional digital modulation is vulnerable to channel impairments, leading to bit errors that cause received tokens to become contextually inconsistent. This paper proposes a receiver-side dual-stage channel-posterior integration framework for masked language model (MLM)-aided token reconstruction. In the proposed framework, the receiver detects unreliable token positions from channel reliability and constructs a vocabulary-level channel-posterior. ArXiv cs.AI.title: SpecRelay: Amortize or Avoid the Round Trip in Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18963v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Edge-cloud speculative decoding moves autoregressive drafting to an edge device while a larger cloud model verifies draft tokens in parallel, so that edge drafting and cloud verification overlap under a synchronous draft-verify schedule. Beyond low-latency local networks, however, the next verification request of that schedule can be sent only after the previous reply arrives, so every round still waits out a full round trip, and throughput falls as the network RTT grows. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Three Invisible Failure Modes in Speech-Based Age Estimation for Child Safety
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated whether three audio-capable large language models can predict a child's age from their speech across five studies using two speech corpora of children under the age of 13. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
ArXiv cs.AI.description:

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to design, optimize, and operate the infrastructure behind AI training and serving, yet the literature remains fragmented across hardware design, machine learning systems, electronic design automation, and high-performance computing.
